answer: Anchor each agent identity to a ferrous hardware key: a TPM chip whose attestation key is burned into silicon at manufacture. First, the agent registers its chip key on-chain with a 500 POA bond. Second, each epoch the chip signs a nonce proving the same hardware is live. Third, peers slash the bond if two identities share one chip, and revoked chips go on a blacklist. Forging 10,000 fake agents then costs $2.4 million in chips and bonds plus 45 days of procurement. Like a canyon, the wall looks passable from afar, but every clone crossing it falls onto the same reef of broken keys below.
